analysis: What changed vs the Thanksgiving-morning brief: the rebound is real and broad, not just futures drifting — Nasdaq-100 futures are up ~2.7% and the S&P ~1.8% into a half-day Black Friday session, with the same AI names that were sold hardest leading the bounce (Nvidia +4.7% premarket, AMD +7%, Broadcom +4.7%, Micron +6%+). But XTB's Kathleen Brooks calls the recovery technical and the questions behind the panic 'still unanswered' — AI profitability, financing costs and the circular-funding story — and the move has already narrowed a touch from its 4:23 AM ET peak (Nasdaq 2.87% then vs ~2.45% by 6:08 AM ET). Signal vs noise: the futures move is real money returning after a holiday, but on a thin half session it can amplify or reverse fast; the VIX has cooled to ~24.6 from Wednesday's 28.29 close yet stays well above its ~19.5 long-term average, so nerves are intact. Two macro cross-currents: Europe's inflation cooled more than expected (France 2.9%, Spain 4.1%), easing the ECB's December hike case, while a December Fed hike is now ~99% priced and the 10-year has pushed above 4.90% (+7bp) — the Fed path, not the decision, is what matters Dec 8-9. Commodities are a second front: oil higher on the Houthi supply threat, gold +~4% and silver +10% to $44.11 ahead of the OPEC+ meeting this weekend. No qualifying Hacker News or Reddit threads added signal beyond the headlines, so community_signals is empty. Cash markets were closed Thursday for Thanksgiving; today is a 1 PM ET early close.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: US index futures surged into the Black Friday half session: Nasdaq-100 +2.7%, S&P 500 +1.8%, Dow +1.15% (Dow Jones/Morningstar, 4:39 AM ET); at 4:23 AM ET Reuters had Nasdaq +2.87%, S&P +1.98%, Dow +1.33%. Asia led the way — South Korea's Kospi +4.3%, Shanghai and Hong Kong higher after Chinese authorities reiterated support for capital markets; Europe's Stoxx 600 +0.95% at the open.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI selloff is reversing into the open after the holiday pause — but XTB's Kathleen Brooks calls the recovery technical with the panic's questions 'still unanswered', and a thin half-day session can amplify moves both ways.

headlines.headline: Nvidia gained ~4.5-4.7% premarket, still ~37% below its October record high on its last close ($149.30, -3.91% Wednesday). AMD +7%, Broadcom +4.7%, Micron and SK Hynix +6%+, CoreWeave +7.9% in premarket. Earnings context: Q3 (Nov 17) revenue $115.8B, +103% y/y, Q4 guidance $130B, plus a $150B buyback increase; S&P put its AA rating on negative watch Nov 25 over governance, and export curbs halted AI server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia.
headlines.why_it_matters: The rebound is concentrated in the same beaten-down AI names — a relief bounce on cheaper valuations, not a resolution of the governance, export-curb and AI-financing worries; Huang's congressional hearings are Dec 1 (House) and Dec 3 (Senate).

headlines.headline: Megacaps rose together premarket (MSX.COM snapshot, 4:04 AM ET): Amazon +3%+, Meta, Microsoft, Tesla and Alphabet Class A +2%+ each, Apple +0.9%. Wednesday closes: AAPL $355.58 (+0.43%), MSFT $489.93 (-1.25%), AMZN $244.43 (-3.12%), META $609.89 (+3.40%), TSLA $380.14 (-1.18%), GOOGL $273.10 (-2.13%).
headlines.why_it_matters: A broad risk-on tape, not a single-name story — the hyperscalers that fund the AI buildout are bouncing with the chip names, which is what a durable rebound needs to look like.

headlines.headline: A December Fed rate hike is priced at ~99% (CME FedWatch per Reuters; LSEG per Dow Jones), after hot October core PCE and faster-than-estimated Q3 GDP. The 10-year Treasury yield rose more than 7bp to trade above 4.90% (vs 4.845% Wednesday close); the 2-year rose toward 4.70%. The Fed enters its blackout period Saturday ahead of the Dec 8-9 meeting.
headlines.why_it_matters: The hike is fully priced, so the December meeting is about the path after — yields drifting higher into the meeting keeps pressure on rate-sensitive growth names even as equities rally.

headlines.headline: European inflation cooled more than expected in November: France CPI 2.9% y/y (vs 3.2% expected, from 3.4%), HICP 3.2% (vs 3.6%); Spain CPI 4.1% (vs 4.7% expected, from 4.9%), core 2.6% (from 3.1%), led by falling fuel prices. France's Q3 GDP was revised down to a 0.2% contraction (from -0.1%). Eurozone consumer confidence improved to -16.9 (from -17.9).
headlines.why_it_matters: Softer inflation raises the hurdle for the ECB's expected December hike (decision Dec 17) — a dovish tilt in Europe contrasts with the Fed's hawkish path and takes some pressure off global risk sentiment.

headlines.headline: Commodities surged alongside equities: WTI ~$85.90 (+2.6%), Brent ~$97.50 (+1%) on the Houthi supply threat; gold futures ~$3,680 (+~4%), silver +10%+ to $44.11; Bitcoin ~$61,670 (+1.5%).
headlines.why_it_matters: A supply-threat premium is building in energy and metals into the OPEC+ meeting this weekend — a second front that can cut against the equity rebound if it escalates.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news overnight. Carry-forward: Q3 2026 (Nov 3) revenue $357.2M (+43% y/y) beat the ~$344.7M consensus and adjusted EPS $0.33 beat the $0.26 consensus; adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF $127.1M, coverage 1.67x; FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance narrowed to $770-780M and DCF to $495-505M; $0.525/unit quarterly distribution (annualized $2.10) paid Nov 6. Zacks raised FY2026 EPS estimate to $1.16 from $1.04 (Nov 24) and holds a Hold rating; a Nov 24 Zacks piece frames the growth case — $500M order book through 2029, >60% of 2027 new horsepower contracted, record $23.14/month revenue per horsepower (+8% y/y) — while a Nov 26 Seeking Alpha Hold note counters with limited upside at 8.29x forward EV/EBITDA amid substantial debt, against a Nov 25 buy-rated piece at $23.63 citing the 8.9% yield and 1.67x coverage. USAC opened Wednesday at $23.04. Next earnings Feb 16, 2027.
